# kwt

> kwt is a Git worktree manager for people and coding agents. It creates one
> isolated checkout per branch, opens a tmux workspace in it, shows the state
> of every worktree across registered projects, and removes worktrees safely.
> The dashboard is for people; the CLI prints JSON for agents and scripts.
> One Go binary; Apache-2.0.

Every page is served as HTML and as Markdown at the same path with a .md
suffix. The Markdown versions are canonical for machine readers.

## Product

- [Product overview](https://kwt.sh/index.md): what kwt does; isolation,
  JSON automation, inert checkouts, interfaces
- [The kwt guide](https://kwt.sh/guide.md): register a project, create
  worktrees, layouts, commands, inspection, pull requests, cleanup, sync,
  embedding

## Docs

- [Documentation index](https://kwt.sh/docs/index.md): what kwt does and where
  each contract is documented
- [Install](https://kwt.sh/docs/get-started/install.md): Go install, release
  archives, source build, shell integration, requirements
- [Quickstart](https://kwt.sh/docs/get-started/quickstart.md): first
  interactive session and first automated worktree
- [Worktree lifecycle and maintenance](https://kwt.sh/docs/workflows/worktree-maintenance.md):
  create, inspect, doctor, prune, remove, and the named safety stops
- [Agent workspaces](https://kwt.sh/docs/workflows/agent-workspaces.md):
  layouts, isolated worktrees, exec, inspection, attachment, cleanup
- [Directory workspaces](https://kwt.sh/docs/workflows/directory-workspaces.md):
  tmux workspaces for directories that are not Git repositories
- [Multi-machine sync](https://kwt.sh/docs/multi-machine-sync.md): advisory
  worktree state across machines through a hub
- [Embed and connect kwt](https://kwt.sh/docs/integrations/embedding.md):
  choosing between CLI, Go services, the local daemon, and the tmux endpoint
- [CLI reference](https://kwt.sh/docs/reference/cli.md): commands, JSON
  fields, exit status, and guarded automation contracts
- [Pull-request automation](https://kwt.sh/docs/reference/pull-requests.md):
  discover, import, inspect, and attach through the protected boundary
- [Configuration](https://kwt.sh/docs/reference/configuration.md):
  config.toml, .kwt.toml trust, layouts, agents, setup, daemon, SSH, fleet
- [Releases](https://kwt.sh/docs/releases.md): versioning and artifacts
- [Changelog](https://kwt.sh/docs/changelog.md): release history
- [Contributing](https://kwt.sh/docs/development/contributing.md): repository
  layout and verification commands
- [Threat model](https://kwt.sh/docs/development/threat-model.md): trusted
  local state versus untrusted branch data
- [Releasing kwt](https://kwt.sh/docs/development/releasing.md): maintainer
  tagging checklist

## Design notes

- [Design notes overview](https://kwt.sh/docs/design/index.md): why each
  contract has its current boundary
- [Local service daemon](https://kwt.sh/docs/design/daemon.md): the
  same-machine lifecycle owner and its client protocol
- [TUI and project registry](https://kwt.sh/docs/design/tui-projects.md):
  dashboard cache, concurrency, and stale-row rules
- [Multi-machine sync architecture](https://kwt.sh/docs/design/multi-machine-sync.md):
  hub, manifests, and freshness
- [Worktree maintenance](https://kwt.sh/docs/design/worktree-maintenance.md):
  doctor and prune internals
- [Worktree change inspection](https://kwt.sh/docs/design/worktree-changes.md):
  generation-bound change snapshots
